content.definition: An algorithmic technique that uses two pointers to traverse a data structure, typically to solve problems in linear time that would otherwise require nested loops.
key_characteristics: Uses two pointers moving through the data structure
Pointers can move in same or opposite directions
Often reduces time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)

opposite_direction.description: Pointers start at opposite ends and move toward each other
opposite_direction.template: left = 0, right = n-1; while left < right: process and move pointers

same_direction.description: Both pointers move in the same direction at different speeds
same_direction.template: slow = 0; for fast in range(n): process and conditionally move slow

fast_slow.description: One pointer moves faster than the other
fast_slow.template: slow = fast = head; move fast 2 steps, slow 1 step per iteration

common_applications.name: Two Sum (Sorted Array)
common_applications.description: Find two numbers that add up to target
common_applications.approach: Use opposite pointers, move based on sum comparison

common_applications.name: Palindrome Verification
common_applications.description: Check if string reads same forwards and backwards
common_applications.approach: Compare characters from both ends moving inward

common_applications.name: Remove Duplicates
common_applications.description: Remove duplicates from sorted array in-place
common_applications.approach: Use read and write pointers moving in same direction

common_applications.name: Cycle Detection
common_applications.approach: Fast pointer moves 2 steps, slow moves 1 step

optimization_strategies: Sort the array first if not already sorted
Use the sorted property to eliminate impossible cases
Skip duplicates to avoid redundant processing
Combine with binary search for enhanced efficiency
common_pitfalls: Off-by-one errors in pointer initialization or movement
Infinite loops when pointers don't converge properly
Not handling edge cases (empty array, single element)
Forgetting to update both pointers when necessary

examples: Brute force two sum: O(n²) → Two pointers: O(n)
Palindrome check with string reversal: O(n) space → Two pointers: O(1) space

interview_recognition: Problems asking for pairs or triplets
advanced_variations: Using with binary search for enhanced complexity
